method: Generated from Docket's shelf, itself built from the hand-curated opportunity register's LOI- and RFP-typed rows. Eligibility is decided by the shelf and read here, never recomputed -- the same rule Almanac follows.
known_limitation: Open-call opportunities are a point-in-time snapshot. Each row was established by hand against the funder's or agency's own page on the date shown, not taken from an aggregator, and a call can still close or change after that check. Confirm the current cycle, deadline and eligibility on the issuing organization's own website before applying.

ready_now.grant_name: AccessLex Institute Grant Programs: Bar Success Research, Bar Success Intervention, Diversity Pathway Intervention, Admission Innovation Project
ready_now.focus_area: Legal education research; bar examination success; law school admission and diversity pathways
ready_now.eligibility: The funder's own Bar Success Research Grant Program page publishes a full dated cycle: 'Letters of Inquiry Accepted Between March 16 and April 20, 2026 (11:59 pm ET)'; 'Proposal Invitation Notification On or before June 23, 2026'; 'Full Proposal Deadline September 1, 2026 (11:59 pm ET)'; 'Funding Invitations Announced On or before November 2, 2026'. The Bar Success Intervention Grant Program page carries the identical 2026 schedule. Fundable projects must 'Have a duration of 12-24 months and seek funding in the amount of $150,000-$300,000' and 'Have a clear research design, using appropriate methodologies'. The grant-programs index states 'We operate four grant programs: the Admission Innovation Project, the Diversity Pathway Intervention Grant Program, the Bar Success Intervention Grant Program, and the Bar Success Research Grant Program. We also support research through an invitation-only Directed Grant Program.' No geographic or organisation-type bar appears on the pages retrieved.
ready_now.notes: Status is open because the funder publishes a complete, dated, recurring application cycle. The close date is deliberately left empty: the entry point for a new applicant is the LOI, whose 2026 window (16 March to 20 April) has already passed, and the 1 September full-proposal deadline applies only to applicants already invited from that LOI round, so recording a deadline here would mislead a new applicant. The program is between windows; the funder has not yet dated the next LOI window. No eligibility bar was found for Measure: the pages state no geographic or organization-type restriction. The real obstacle is subject matter, not eligibility; every program concerns legal education, the bar exam, or law school admission, none of which is a Measure program area (community-led data, public-safety accountability, racial equity research, maternal health equity). A partnership with a law school on an evaluation design is conceivable but not a natural fit.

ready_now.grant_name: Just Futures Initiative, rolling grant opportunity for grassroots community-safety and democracy organisations, $50,000 to $200,000
ready_now.eligibility: Funder's own page, re-checked 2026-08-11: header now explicitly states [CLOSED], no reopening date given -- was open as of the prior determination.
ready_now.notes: This is a philanthropic intermediary hosting donor-collaborative pooled funds that regrant, not a donor-advised fund sponsor. At least one fund it hosts runs an open, quiz-then-LOI application route for organizations it does not already know. Measure is plausibly eligible and this is a genuine prospect: it is a US 501(c)(3) in Austin, Travis County, Texas, and its public-safety data and accountability practice sits squarely in the Just Futures subject area, with no geographic restriction stated. Two conditions Measure would need to clear: a budget under $2 million, and being 'rooted in communities impacted by criminalization'; both should be checked against Measure's current financials before applying. Caveat: this fund hosts many programs, and most of the others are nomination- or invitation-based; this assessment is specific to the Just Futures Initiative, not the host organization as a whole.

ready_now.grant_name: IRUSA Domestic Grant Program, ongoing rolling application for US non-profits across food security, healthcare, livelihood and community development
ready_now.focus_area: Food security; healthcare for underserved populations; livelihood and self-sufficiency including career development, ESL and citizenship classes; community development including domestic violence intervention, youth programmes and capacity building
ready_now.eligibility: PRIOR CLOSE OVERTURNED. Islamic Relief USA's own US Programs grant page sets out an open door with published eligibility: 'The organization is an IRS registered 501(c)(3) public charity in good standing'; 'The organization has been active for 3 full calendar years in the United States'; 'The organization's proposed project's activities and funds must be distributed exclusively within the US'; an annual cash budget under $3 million (stated as strongly desired rather than disqualifying); and 'The organization is not seeking funding to conduct direct religious activities or services'. Programming must be in the contiguous 48 states. On timing IRUSA states 'The IRUSA Domestic Grant application is an ongoing process with no fixed annual deadlines', so close_date is empty and that emptiness correctly means ROLLING here. Route in for an organisation not already known to IRUSA: contact the Grants Team at usgrants@irusa.org for an initial meeting, then register on the IRUSA FLUXX platform, submit an organisational profile with non-profit documentation, submit a Concept Note after staff review, and if selected submit a full Program Proposal on FLUXX.
ready_now.notes: This is an operating relief charity that also runs a competitive domestic partner-grants program: the regranting to service partners IS the competitive program, with published eligibility, four named priority categories, and a staged concept-note-to-proposal process open to organizations it does not already know. Measure clears the stated bars: US 501(c)(3), located in the contiguous 48 states, formed well before the three-full-calendar-year threshold, and seeking no funding for religious activity; the under-$3-million budget preference should be checked against current financials. Program fit is the live question rather than eligibility. Measure's maternal health equity work maps to the Healthcare category and its community-led data and capacity work could be framed under Community Development, but IRUSA's stated healthcare emphasis is on direct service by licensed nonprofits filling service gaps, so a pure research, data, and evaluation proposal is a stretch and would need a service partner. Note also that the explicit no-direct-religious-activity condition does not bar secular applicants; it bars religious programming.

ready_now.grant_name: NEO Philanthropy collaborative funds run episodic OPEN RFPs alongside a default no-unsolicited-requests policy; Economic Mobility and Opportunity Fund most recent verified call, now closed
ready_now.focus_area: Immigration, democracy and voting, reproductive justice, racial justice, climate justice and LGBTQ rights through collaborative funds; the Economic Mobility and Opportunity Fund call was specifically for research and data advancing economic mobility
ready_now.eligibility: PRIOR CLOSE OVERTURNED, with the qualification stated plainly rather than buried. NEO Philanthropy's own FAQ states 'NEO Philanthropy does not accept unsolicited grant requests or proposals', and describes building relationships through its collaborative funds and typically inviting organisations to apply. THAT IS THE DEFAULT, NOT THE WHOLE PICTURE. NEO's own site also publishes competitive open calls under its collaborative funds, with public eligibility and an online application, which means the brief's closed test, invitation-only with no door for any new applicant, is not met. The most recent verified example is NEO's own announcement that 'The EMO Fund announces a $2.3 million opportunity for organizations focused on research and data in support of advancing economic mobility and opportunity', open to US-based 501(c)(3) non-profits with annual budgets of $2 million or less, with awards of '$100,000 - $300,000' for one year with possibility of a no-cost extension, two tracks (Sustainability and Capacity Building, and Innovation and Imagination), a Letter of Interest deadline of 31 October 2025 and a full RFP deadline in January 2026. BOTH OF THOSE DATES HAVE PASSED as of 2026-08-03, so that specific call is over and close_date is left empty; the emptiness here means no current call is dated, NOT rolling. NEO's collaborative funds page names the Four Freedoms Fund and the State Infrastructure Fund and states nothing about their application status either way, so nothing is claimed for them. A separate fiscal-sponsorship application route exists for projects whose work aligns with NEO's mission and meets its budget requirements.
ready_now.notes: This is a donor-collaborative intermediary and fiscal sponsor. This is the highest-value watch item in this review for Measure specifically: the Economic Mobility and Opportunity Fund's stated criteria describe Measure almost exactly, a US 501(c)(3) with a budget at or under $2 million doing research and data work, and its award band of $100,000 to $300,000 in one-year general operating support would be transformative at Measure's scale. Measure could not have applied to the now-closed cycle but should watch for the next round and for any comparable call from the collaborative's other funds. Not eligible today only because no call is presently open; a timing bar, not a bar on Measure. The practical route in the meantime, as the fund itself describes, is direct contact and relationship-building with fund staff, since invitation is the normal path in.
